ai.title: Usage limit warning skips paid subscriptions
ai.summary: Added `!a.subscription_active` check to the usage limit warning condition in `npm-app/src/client.ts`. Prevents 'exceeded monthly usage limit' console output for users with active paid subscriptions. Scope limited to CLI client warning logic.

eli5.text: When you reached the monthly usage limit on the command-line tool, it used to print a message telling you to upgrade your plan. Now, if your account already has an active paid subscription, that warning is skipped entirely so you won't see the upgrade prompt. This only affects the warning shown in the terminal; all actual usage limits and billing remain unchanged. The change is live today for anyone who pays for a subscription.

If you use the AI coding assistant, you may notice that the warning about hitting a usage limit will no longer appear for paid subscribers. Behind the scenes, the software's version label was bumped, which is what packages this set of improvements and ships them to your installation. This is already live today for anyone who installs or updates to the new version.

ai.title: Fix CLI usage warning consistency
ai.summary: Refactored `showUsageWarning` in `npm-app/src/client.ts` to ensure `returnControlToUser` is called immediately upon receiving a usage response, preventing potential UI hangs. Consolidated upgrade and referral messaging into a single block with updated `picocolors` styling. Removed duplicate limit-check logic from the message handler in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to prevent conflicting warnings. Added a Konami code easter egg handler in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: The command-line warning you see when you hit your usage limit is now shown consistently every time, without delay or duplication. When the tool tells you about running low on credits, it immediately gives you back control of the terminal and presents a single, clearer message about upgrading or referring friends, rather than potentially freezing or showing the warning twice. Behind the scenes, developers also added a hidden Konami code (uuddlrlrba) that triggers a fun animated easter egg drawing the Claude logo in the terminal, though that's just a playful addition for anyone who enters the code.

ai.title: Raise MAXITERATIONS to 15 and fix empty continuation
ai.summary: MAX_ITERATIONS in backend/src/main-prompt.ts increases from 5 to 15. The 'continuing to generate' logic now checks if fullResponseMinusLastLine.trim() is non-empty before setting continuedMessages, otherwise resets it to []. This prevents malformed continuation prompts when responses consist solely of whitespace or are empty.

eli5.text: You may notice the assistant now keeps working on a response for a longer time before giving up, so longer or more involved answers are less likely to stop mid-sentence. You would also notice that if the assistant gets cut off and starts to continue, it no longer sends a broken or incomplete follow-up message when there is nothing meaningful left to say. These changes apply to anyone using the assistant today, with no special steps required.
